query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended for structural use under extreme-temperature conditions, what single intervention could improve high-temperature oxygen resistance? State one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to the untreated alloy, defines the temperature, atmosphere, and exposure conditions under which it should work, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adding 0.5 at.% of Yttrium (Y) to a refractory high-entropy alloy will improve its high-temperature oxygen resistance by forming a protective Y2O3 oxide layer, reducing the oxidation rate by 30% relative to the untreated alloy at 1000°C in an oxidizing atmosphere.
generation.mechanism: scavenging oxygen and forming a protective oxide layer
generation.uncertainty: The actual improvement in oxygen resistance may vary depending on the specific alloy composition and processing conditions.

falsification_experiment.design: expose both untreated and Y-added refractory high-entropy alloys to 1000°C in an oxidizing atmosphere for 100 hours and measure the oxidation rate
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: if the oxidation rate of the Y-added alloy is not at least 20% lower than that of the untreated alloy, the hypothesis is falsified
